newsitem.title: USA: California Senator backs controversial tax measure.
newsitem.headline: California Senator backs controversial tax measure.

text.p: A prominent California state Senator on Friday said he supported a controversial tax measure that would make it more difficult for local governments to impose taxes, fees and assessments.
Quentin Kopp, an Independent state senator from San Francisco, said in a statement that Proposition 218 would empower voters by giving them the right to approve all taxes.

"Approval of new taxes should be decided by people, not bureaucrats or politicians," Kopp said in the statement. "Quite simply, a Yes vote on Proposition 218 will afford people the right to vote on new taxes."
Kopp said assessments and fees imposed by local government agencies have increased dramatically in recent years.
"Proposition 218 may be our last hope to stop runaway taxation," Kopp said. "If government agencies build a good case for an increase, taxpayers will approve it."

Municipal analysts have warned that Proposition 218 would constrain local governments' ability to impose fees, assessments and taxes. The measure would apply to all cities, counties, special districts, redevelopment agencies and school districts in California.
While the measure would reduce the amount of fees and taxes that individuals and businesses pay, it would decrease spending for local public services, analysts said.
Earlier on Friday, Fitch Investors Service Inc warned that the proposition, if approved by California voters on November 5, would have a negative effect on municipal credit quality.
